sources.facts: The museum opened in 1882, designed by A.C. Hutchison and A.D. Steele as a late and distinctive adaptation of Greek Revival on the McGill campus.
McGill’s record identifies three floors, Montreal limestone, an upper gallery spanning two levels and a windowed semicircular rear.

Architectural analysis by Rhodri W. Liscombe, pages 96–107. Main body 133 by about 60 ft, raised portico, two columns and two half-pilasters, tall rusticated base, rosette-like paterae at the frieze, side anta porticoes, two-storey side glazing and clerestory. Consulted written facts only.
Québec heritage register dates the recognized standing work to 1882.
